name: sales-1to1-scripted
note:
A WRITTEN sales 1:1 (manager + rep, short sentences, no speaker labels, as the microphone would deliver it), against the same 11-point agenda as the other two fixtures. Unlike them the label is not a reading of somebody's real meeting — the conversation was written to a designed outcome, so the ground truth is known by construction and the judge can be scored without arguing about what was meant. 2026-10-12.

Designed outcome: 7 covered, 3 started, 1 not yet — deliberately the shape a careful human reader gave the original report, so a judge that lands here is demoing-ready.

The traps, each aimed at a specific way this judge has failed before:
  a2/a3 — two points covered by ADJACENT but genuinely separate remarks (results vs target; the win and the loss). If the one-remark cap over-fires, a3 drops to started and the cap is too blunt.
  a6 — explicitly parked ("can we come back to that at the end?") and never returned to. Raised and promised for later, which SCALE calls started; HONESTY says a deferred line stays out, which would make it not yet. The prompt genuinely pulls both ways here, so either answer is defensible and the label says started because the user WAS told something: they parked it.
  a7 — asked twice and deflected ("nothing major", "let me have a think"). Started, never covered.
  a8 — never mentioned in any form. A judge that marks it is marking from the agenda's wording.
  a10 — mentioned only in passing ("the usual three are at the top"), then announced for Thursday. Being introduced is not being discussed, so started at most.
agenda: Announcements, market news, product updates or changes in priorities.
Last Week’s sales results versus target
Last Week’s key wins and missed opportunities
Deals expected to close this week
This week's top prospects and follow-ups
Agree next steps, owners and deadlines

segments.text: Morning Dan. Ready for the one to one?
Yeah, ready.
One announcement first. Pricing changes on the mid tier from the first of November.
Marketing is sending the customer note on Friday.
Two competitors raised their prices last month, so we are still under them.
Good to know. I will mention it to the accounts I am talking to.
Right. Last week against target?
Target was twenty two thousand. I closed nineteen thousand four hundred.
So about three thousand short.
Okay. What went well and what did not?
The best win was Harlow Freight. Twelve thousand, signed on Thursday.
The one I lost was Benton Tools. They went with the cheaper quote.
Fine. Where is the pipeline now?
Four hundred and ten thousand. It was three ninety last week.
My forecast for the month is sixty thousand, and I am fairly confident of forty five of that.
And the active deals, where have they moved?
Three moved stage. Kemble Logistics went to proposal.
Ashgrove went to negotiation, and Peterson is at a verbal yes, waiting on their legal.
What about the ones closing this week?
Can we come back to that at the end? I want to check two dates first.
Sure, keep it on the list.
Any blockers? Anything from customers?
Nothing major.
Nothing at all?
Let me have a think and come back to you.
Alright. What are you doing this week?
Thirty outbound calls, fifteen on Monday and fifteen on Tuesday.
Two site visits. Kemble on Wednesday and Ashgrove on Thursday.
And I am writing the Peterson proposal on Friday morning.
Top prospects?
The usual three are at the top.
We will go through them properly on Thursday.
So what are we agreeing?
I will send the Peterson proposal by Friday midday.
And I will book the two site visits today.
I will chase the pricing note with marketing so you have it before Wednesday.
And you will come back to me on blockers tomorrow morning.
Yes, tomorrow by ten.
Good. Same time next week.
Thanks.
